title: Hilary Duff Announces 2027 North American Tour
seoTitle: Hilary Duff Announces 2027 North American Tour
subtitle: Shows Kick Off October 1st in Florida and Conclude November 20th in California
excerpt: Singer-actress Hilary Duff has expanded her Lucky Me Tour with 32 new dates across North America, Europe, and Latin America, starting October 1st in Sunrise, FL.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Hilary Duff has officially announced the dates for the 2027 extension of her Lucky Me Tour, including 32 performances across the United States, Europe, and Latin America. The announcement comes after the artist concluded her show at London's O2 Arena with a "2027 More Dates Loading" message for fans.

North American Tour Kick-off

The first U.S. stop is on October 1st at the Amerant Bank Arena in Sunrise, Florida. The sequence includes cities such as Orlando (FL), Raleigh (NC), Baltimore (MD), and others, continuing until the tour concludes on November 20th at the Honda Center in Anaheim, California.

Confirmed Cities and Dates

  • Oct 1 – Sunrise, FL – Amerant Bank Arena
  • Oct 2 – Orlando, FL – Kia Center
  • Oct 4 – Raleigh, NC – Lenovo Center
  • Oct 6 – Baltimore, MD – CFG Bank Arena
  • Oct 8 – Uncasville, CT – Mohegan Sun Arena
  • Oct 9 – Hershey, PA – Giant Center
  • Oct 11 – Buffalo, NY – KeyBank Center
  • Oct 13 – Cleveland, OH – Rocket Arena
  • Oct 15 – Columbus, OH – Schottenstein Center
  • Oct 16 – Pittsburgh, PA – PPG Paints Arena
  • Nov 5 – San Antonio, TX – Frost Bank Center
  • Nov 6 – Fort Worth, TX – Dickies Arena
  • Nov 8 – Tulsa, OK – BOK Center
  • Nov 10 – Omaha, NE – CHI Health Center
  • Nov 12 – Milwaukee, WI – Fiserv Forum
  • Nov 14 – Des Moines, IA – Casey’s Center
  • Nov 15 – Kansas City, MO – T-Mobile Center
  • Nov 17 – Denver, CO – Ball Arena
  • Nov 20 – Anaheim, CA – Honda Center

Opening Acts

Supporting acts for the North American performances will be Dashboard Confessional and Tegan and Sara. General tickets go on sale October 2nd.

Album and Tour Context

The tour accompanies the album "Luck…or Something," released earlier this year, the artist's first record in over a decade. Since its release, Duff has performed in various cities, including two nights at Madison Square Garden in New York.

Artist's Statements

In an interview with Rolling Stone, Duff stated that she didn't want the new album to be defined solely by her role as a mother, but rather by how the music makes her feel as a person, describing the process as "super healing."

With information from Rolling Stone.
